Plot one metric, a length screen or TUBELEX coverage

plot.lexdiv_results.Rd

Draws a single measurement specification and invisibly returns its selected rows. Different metrics or parameter settings are not combined on one scale.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_results'
plot(x, metric_id = NULL, request_id = NULL,
  col = NULL, pch = 19, main = NULL, xlab = "", ylab = NULL, ...,
  monochrome = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_batch_results'
plot(x, metric_id = NULL, request_id = NULL,
  col = NULL, pch = 19, main = NULL, xlab = "", ylab = NULL, ...,
  monochrome = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_profile_results'
plot(x, metric_id = NULL, request_id = NULL,
  col = NULL, pch = 19, main = NULL, xlab = "", ylab = NULL, ...,
  monochrome = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_profile_batch_results'
plot(x, metric_id = NULL,
  request_id = NULL, col = NULL, pch = 19, main = NULL, xlab = "",
  ylab = NULL, ..., monochrome = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_text_results'
plot(x, ..., monochrome = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_screen_results'
plot(x, screen_id = NULL, col = NULL,
  pch = 19, main = NULL, xlab = "document / request", ylab = "tokens",
  ..., monochrome = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'tubelex_profile'
plot(x, col = "#0072B2", main = NULL,
  ylab = "coverage", ..., monochrome = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A supported lexical-diversity, length-screen or TUBELEX result.

metric_id

One exact metric ID. May be omitted only for a single-metric result.

request_id

An optional profile request ID to select.

screen_id

One screen ID. May be omitted only for a single-screen result.

col, pch, main, xlab, ylab

Base-graphics settings. Metric points below the advisory token floor are orange triangles; other finite results are blue circles. Explicit pch overrides the default symbols.

monochrome

One TRUE or FALSE; specify by name. TRUE overrides col with black (gray for TUBELEX bars). Point symbols are retained. Defaults to color.

...

Additional base-graphics arguments, including axes, xaxt, cex.axis, family, las and bty. TUBELEX bars use fixed category labels and a fixed zero-to-one scale; height, horiz, offset, add, log, plot, ylim and names.arg are rejected for that plot.

Value

The selected data frame, invisibly. Metric plots retain missing rows as well as computed rows. Original results are unchanged.

Details

Metric plots require a single specification, including when all rows share the same metric ID. Select a request or subset the input by specification. Their invisible return contains label followed by the complete selected result rows, including parameter and contract columns. Only finite rows with status = "ok" receive points. Other rows retain their horizontal positions labelled “not computed”; they are not drawn at zero. All selected rows participate in the specification check. A selection with no finite ok value raises an error. TUBELEX plots show token- and type-weighted match coverage on a fixed zero-to-one scale. All plot methods return the plotted data invisibly for testing and reuse. Plots have no automatic title. A sans serif font, horizontal tick labels and an open frame are used by default. Override these with family, las or bty in ...; cosmetic graphics parameters are restored after drawing, including after an error. The default metric y-axis label is the uppercase metric ID, except for “TTR (V/N)”. Place figure numbers, titles and notes outside the image in the manuscript. Explicit main remains available for custom base graphics. TTR uses a zero-to-one scale by default (override with ylim) and includes token counts in the horizontal labels. Equal measurement specifications do not make unequal-length TTR values comparable. TTR has no advisory token floor; a blue circle does not establish adequate precision. For length diagnostics use a scatterplot of N against value, retaining task and writer information. For large batches, use explicit grouped plots instead of crowded document labels. See the installed choosing-metrics guide for controlled-length evidence and sampling reliability. plot.lexdiv_text_results() delegates to the unchanged results component, so it accepts the same metric-selection arguments and does not plot preprocessing coverage on a metric scale.

axes = FALSE suppresses both axes; xaxt = "n" suppresses only the horizontal axis, including manually drawn document labels. cex.axis, col.axis and font.axis also apply to those labels. Graphics settings are restored after drawing or an error.

See also

lexdiv_widen, nj8_profile, plot.lexdiv_mattr_profile, lexdiv_reference_coverage, lexdiv_concordance.

Examples

long <- lexdiv_metrics_batch(list(a = c("one", "two", "one"),
  empty = character(), b = c("one", "two", "three")),
  metrics = c("ttr", "maas"))
plot(long, metric_id = "ttr")

plot(long, metric_id = "ttr", monochrome = TRUE, cex.axis = 0.9)

text_result <- lexdiv_metrics_text("Words repeat words.", metrics = "ttr")
plot(text_result)


# Only this optional profile needs downloaded reference data.
if (lexdiv_resource_info("tubelex")$available) {
  profile <- tubelex_profile(c("the", "not-in-resource"))
  plot(profile)
}
